title: The Grid and the Medianera: Caseros, the Subte Centennial, and the Idols at Full Height
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Caseros, birth beside the San Martín line
stops.date_confidence: attested; full date given by es.wikipedia, 'Martín Ron (artista)'
stops.campa: A son is born in Caseros, cabecera of the partido of Tres de Febrero, where the General San Martín line runs west out of the capital and the town arranges itself along the rails. Buenos Aires proper is forty minutes away and holds the museums; Caseros holds freight yards, factory flanks, station gables, and long blind medianeras thrown up by builders who never expected anyone to look at them. They name him Martín Ron. He will spend a working life on surfaces of exactly that kind, and will keep this district as his base long after the world starts sending for him.
suggested_refs: Caseros, cabecera of the Partido de Tres de Febrero, Buenos Aires Province

stops.name: UNTREF, the degree in managing art
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source; the year is set only to place the studies before the teaching that follows, and carries no evidential weight
stops.campa: The Universidad Nacional de Tres de Febrero stands in the district he was born in, and he enrolls there to study gestión en arte y cultura: the administration of art rather than its technique. Painters do not usually take that degree. He will later run a municipal mural program and put twenty-five artists to work on the pillars of a motorway, which is permits and scheduling long before it is paint. He learns the paperwork of culture in the town where he will spend it. No source gives the years of the degree.
suggested_refs: Universidad Nacional de Tres de Febrero, carrera de Gestión de Arte y Cultura

stops.name: UNTREF, the muralismo course
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source; placed before the 2010 municipal program on the sequence given by es.wikipedia, not on any dated record
stops.campa: He comes back to the same university as a teacher, running courses in muralismo for students who will paint walls in the same partido. What he has to teach is scale. A face drawn at arm's length behaves differently at forty metres, read from a moving car, and a grid laid over a photograph may or may not survive being enlarged four hundred times. The facade sets its own limits before anyone opens a can. He leaves the university later and runs his own seminars and workshops instead.
suggested_refs: The muralism seminars Ron ran independently after leaving UNTREF

segments.name: Embellecimiento Urbano: the District as Gallery

stops.name: Tres de Febrero, artistic director of Embellecimiento Urbano
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 2010; month and day not recorded, defaulted to 01
stops.campa: From 2010 he is artistic director of Embellecimiento Urbano, a mural program of the municipality that raised him. The arrangement is unusual for a painter of his generation: not gallery representation but a standing commission from a local government. School walls, underpasses, station gables, the sides of houses. With his collaborators the count passes two hundred and fifty murals across the partido and keeps climbing. The walls stand in Tres de Febrero, in the province. Later accounts of his career quietly move them into the capital.
suggested_refs: Programa Embellecimiento Urbano, Municipio de Tres de Febrero

stops.name: Caseros, the wall against the tracks
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source, which is a photograph caption; the year is a placeholder inside the municipal program period and is not evidence
stops.campa: He paints a wall in his own town, hard against the General San Martín tracks, where the commuter trains pass it every few minutes. Riders get two seconds of it going in and two seconds coming back, and within a week they have stopped seeing it at all. The railway is the reason Caseros exists: the yards laid out the streets and the town grew along them afterwards. He is decorating the machine that built the ground he was born on, on the one surface in the district everybody passes and nobody stops at.
suggested_refs: The Ferrocarril General San Martín right-of-way through Caseros

stops.name: Barrio Ejército de los Andes, the Tévez wall
stops.date_confidence: the individual mural is undated; only the start of the icon series is dated to 2011 by Clarín, so this year orders the sequence and does not date the wall
stops.campa: In the housing blocks of Ejército de los Andes, called Fuerte Apache by everyone including the people who live in it, he paints Carlos Tévez on a wall of the barrio Tévez was born in. The complex reaches the papers for poverty and shootings, and also for the footballers it exports. A portrait here puts the barrio in charge of its own picture: its most famous son at the height of a building, painted from inside rather than described from outside. No source fixes the block or the date.
suggested_refs: Barrio Ejército de los Andes (Fuerte Apache), Ciudadela, Partido de Tres de Febrero
sources: Clarín, 'Arte urbano: homenajes en los muros a los ídolos populares', Nahuel Gallot

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the series of popular idols
stops.date_confidence: attested for the start of the series in 2011; no individual mural in it is dated by any reachable source
stops.campa: From 2011 he works with other painters on a series of oversized tributes to popular idols, faces the country already carries: Diego Maradona, the actress Isabel Sarli, the cuarteto singer La Mona Jiménez of Córdoba. The walls go up hyperrealist and enormous on facades that no institution selected and no curator approved. The press names the figures and not the addresses. Where the Sarli and the La Mona murals stand, in what year each was painted, and whether either still exists, no reachable source says.
suggested_refs: Clarín's 2011 survey of Buenos Aires murals honouring popular idols
sources: Clarín, 'Arte urbano: homenajes en los muros a los ídolos populares', Nahuel Gallot

segments.name: Meeting of Styles and the First Wall Abroad

stops.name: Barracas, Pedro de Luján y su perro
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2012 by the BA Street Art interview of November 2012; the month of painting is not recorded
stops.campa: On a factory facade on Pedro de Luján street in Barracas he paints the second edition of Meeting of Styles Buenos Aires, having painted the first as well. An old man sits at the bottom of the wall with his dog; above him a sea turtle comes flying out of a hole broken in the brick, hyperrealist and three-dimensional. The mural takes its title from the street it stands on. In 2017 the wall is demolished. The interview that recorded the turtle is now the only reachable account of a piece that made his name in this city.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires Street Art interview with Ron on the Meeting of Styles wall, November 2012
sources: buenosairesstreetart.com, interview with Martín Ron, November 2012 (records the Pedro de Luján location and the 2017 demolition)

stops.name: Glauchau, the Ibug festival
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2012; Ibug is held in late summer, but no date is given by the source
stops.campa: His first trip out of Argentina lands in a small Saxon town given over for a week to Ibug, a festival that takes abandoned industrial buildings and hands them to painters. European street art at the time runs to letterforms and looser figuration; he arrives with a photographic grid and a habit of scale learned on suburban medianeras. The buildings are slated for demolition or conversion, so the work is temporary by design. It is the first wall outside his country to carry his name, and nothing reachable records which building it was.
suggested_refs: Ibug Festival für Kultur und urbane Kunst, Glauchau, Saxony

stops.name: Congreso, a hundred faces on a Línea A formation
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013 by Clarín; the exact date of the painting is not recorded
stops.campa: The subte turns a hundred, the first underground railway in Latin America, and he paints an entire Línea A formation for the anniversary. A hundred Argentine faces run the length of the cars: Julio Cortázar, Mercedes Sosa, Juan Manuel Fangio, Luis Alberto Spinetta, Carlos Tévez, shoulder to shoulder on steel that never stops moving. The train keeps its ordinary service. Passengers do not visit this gallery; they ride inside it, and it runs under the city all day and returns to the yards at night.
suggested_refs: The 'Cien años del Subterráneo' centennial program, Buenos Aires, 1913-2013
sources: Clarín, 'Pintan retratos de ídolos de la cultura popular en los vagones de la línea A', Nahuel Gallot

stops.name: Plaza de Mayo station, painting under the square
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013 as part of the station program; the individual station work is undated
stops.campa: The terminus of the oldest line sits under the square where every government in the country's modern history has been cheered or besieged. He paints in the station during the centennial year, a wall for people crossing the exact point at which the ordinary commute and the national stage share a roof. Above, the Casa Rosada and the weekly circuit of the mothers around the pyramid; below, tiling from another century's idea of the future, and a painter working between trains.
suggested_refs: Plaza de Mayo station, Línea A, Subte de Buenos Aires

stops.name: Plaza Miserere station, the heaviest traffic in the city
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013 as part of the station program; the individual station work is undated
stops.campa: Plaza Miserere is the other end of the same line, the station that feeds Once, its terminal buses and the densest street market in the city. Nobody calls it beautiful. He paints here in the centennial year, putting hyperrealist work into a hall whose crowds pass at the speed of people with trains to catch. It is the busiest interchange in the network and among the least regarded, and the painting is seen almost entirely by people who did not come to look at anything.
suggested_refs: Plaza Miserere station, Línea A, and the Once transport hub

stops.name: Medrano station, the columns of Línea B
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013; the column intervention is undated within that year
stops.campa: At Medrano he takes the platform, and then the support columns of Línea B itself, painting them in a chromatic gradient calculated for a moving eye. Standing still, it is a row of coloured pillars. Seen from a train at speed it becomes a single sweep of colour running the length of the tunnel, an effect that exists only for passengers and only while they are in motion. The trick is as old as animation itself. He runs it underground, on structural columns nobody ever meant anyone to look at.
suggested_refs: The painted support columns of Línea B, Subte de Buenos Aires

stops.name: Hospitales station, Tita Merello and Ángel Villoldo
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013 through the city government's Paseo Cultural del Tango; no month recorded
stops.campa: For the city's Paseo Cultural del Tango he paints Hospitales station in Parque Patricios with Tita Merello and Ángel Villoldo: the woman who sang the tango in the voice of the arrabal, and the man who wrote El Choclo. The work is not his alone. The station's own record credits it to Martín Ron and Leandro Frizzero, a joint authorship the summaries of his career quietly drop. Those summaries also put the station on Línea A. It stands on Línea H, on the other side of the city.
suggested_refs: Hospitales station (now Hospitales-Ringo Bonavena), Línea H, Av. Almafuerte 300, Parque Patricios
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Hospitales (Subte de Buenos Aires)' (credits Ron and Leandro Frizzero)

stops.name: Villa Urquiza, El cuento de los loros
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2013; no month or day recorded in any reachable source
stops.campa: On a four-storey medianera in Villa Urquiza he paints El cuento de los loros over four hundred and twelve square metres, parrots at a size that turns a residential building into a landmark for the blocks around it. It is the largest mural in that barrio to date and the largest he has yet painted, an initiative of a street-art organisation working with the city government, which is the arrangement that will carry him abroad within a year. The exact street address is not recorded in anything reachable.
suggested_refs: 'El cuento de los loros', Villa Urquiza, 412 m2, commissioned through BA Street Art and the Buenos Aires city government
sources: Clarín, 'El mural más grande, en Villa Urquiza', Nora Sánchez

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Proyecto Dúo with Nase Pop
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2014; no month recorded
stops.campa: Twelve painters are paired into duos for Proyecto Dúo, each made to share a wall with a hand that is not their own. He is paired with Nase Pop. The arrangement works against his method: a hyperrealist grid wants total command of the surface, a photograph enlarged square by square, and a second hand on the same wall is a variable it cannot absorb. No reachable source records what the two of them painted, where in the city the wall stood, or whether it is still standing.
suggested_refs: Proyecto Dúo, the twelve-artist pairing project, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Wynwood, Miami: From Argentina with Love
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2014 through the gallery's own exhibition page, seen via the Wayback Machine; no month recorded
stops.campa: His work travels to Miami for a group show at a gallery in Wynwood, the warehouse district that rebuilt its economy on painted walls. The register changes: hyperrealism scaled down from a building to a room, framed and priced. The show is called From Argentina with Love and sells the nationality along with the canvases. Wynwood is one of the few American districts where a muralist arrives already legible to buyers, having been sold to them as a neighbourhood of walls. The precise address of the gallery is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Vice Gallery, 'From Argentina with Love', Wynwood, Miami
sources: Vice Gallery exhibition page, archived via the Wayback Machine

stops.name: Werchter, the tower of containers
stops.date_confidence: contested: the source cited for this event gives no year at all, one research lens dates it 2014 and another 2015; 2014 is used here only to hold the sequence and the contradiction is not resolved
stops.campa: At Rock Werchter, in a Flemish village that swells to a hundred thousand people for four days each summer, he paints for North West Walls, the shipping-container project curated by Arne Quinze. The tower is stacked steel boxes rather than a wall: a man's head, a parrot on a branch held in his mouth, carried across seams and corrugations that break every straight line a grid depends on. The containers come apart when the festival does. He is painting to a four-day deadline, on a support built to be taken down.
suggested_refs: North West Walls, the container-tower street art project at Rock Werchter, curated by Arne Quinze
sources: arnequinze.com, 'North West Walls Street Art Project', cited via es.wikipedia; the page and its Wayback copy were unreachable in this research pass

stops.name: Ely's Yard, London: the burning crown
stops.date_confidence: the blog that records the wall was published 5 August 2015 and describes the painting as done 'last Saturday and Sunday', so the work falls in late July or the first days of August; the date here is that window, not a documented day
stops.campa: Off Hanbury Street, in the yards of a brewery that stopped making beer and became a market with walls for rent, he paints across a weekend: a man's head inside a circular checkerboard, the crown of it engulfed in flame. A London blog logs it days after the paint dries. He is not new to this quarter, having painted nearby before, once alongside the Belgian animal painter ROA on Hanbury Street itself. The address his career summaries give for this wall belongs to a different corner of the brewery.
suggested_refs: London Calling Blog, 'New Martin Ron Work In The Truman Brewery', 5 August 2015
sources: London Calling Blog, 5 August 2015 (locates the wall at Ely's Place / Ely's Yard, not the 'Colbert Place' given by es.wikipedia)

stops.name: Hackney Wick, Number 90
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2015 by es.wikipedia and by an August 2015 blog report of work in progress; no completion date recorded
stops.campa: In the warehouse quarter along the River Lea, where former industrial units hold artists' studios and the walls have been a continuous open gallery for a decade, he paints at Number 90 on Wallis Road. The piece is recorded under the name Machaco. It is not a solo wall: he works it with Jiant, another Argentine painter in London that season, which makes the wall two hands from the same city rather than one visitor among British and European ones. The summaries of his career credit him alone and lose the second name.
suggested_refs: Number 90, Wallis Road, Hackney Wick, London E9
sources: London Calling Blog, 5 August 2015 (reports the Hackney Wick wall as a collaboration with Jiant)
es.wikipedia, 'Martín Ron (artista)' (supplies the title 'Machaco' and the year)

stops.name: Bedminster, Bristol: Andromeda
stops.date_confidence: single-sourced to es.wikipedia for the year; the festival's own listings name neither the painter nor the work, so both date and attribution are unconfirmed
stops.campa: Bristol treats painted walls as civic heritage and hands North Street in Bedminster and Southville over each summer to Upfest, the largest free street-art festival in Europe. A mural called Andromeda is recorded to him there. The festival's own listings name neither the work nor the painter, so the attribution rests on a single line in an encyclopedia article and on nothing else, and the wall has not been located. He is in England this year for three murals, and this is counted as the third of them.
suggested_refs: Upfest, the Urban Paint Festival, North Street, Bedminster, Bristol

stops.name: Mayfair, the solo show at Mead Carney
stops.date_confidence: no source gives a year; grouped with the 2015 London walls by inference only, and the inference is weak
stops.campa: A solo exhibition in Mayfair, in the gallery district where a London art career is priced rather than photographed, puts him indoors and behind glass a few miles from the brewery yard. The same grid, the same hyperrealism, bounded now by a frame and by opening hours. It is his second exhibition anywhere. The year is not recorded, the gallery's own website has decayed into a parked directory, and even the street is disputed: an encyclopedia says Cork Street, the trade record says Dover Street.
suggested_refs: Mead Carney Fine Art, Mayfair, London
sources: meadcarney.com (checked; resolves to a parked WordPress file listing)
artsy.net gallery record (HTTP 403 in this research pass)

stops.name: Tallinn, Mudra
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2015 by es.wikipedia only; no month, and no independent confirmation
stops.campa: He paints a large wall in Tallinn and calls it Mudra, after the Sanskrit word for the ritual positions of the hands. The Baltic has no tradition of what he does and no obvious use for it, which is part of why the invitation comes at all: the technique reads as an event wherever it has not been seen. In one year he works in England, Estonia, Malaysia and the Canary Islands, painting at building height in four climates and living out of a case of cans. The building carrying Mudra is named in no reachable source.
suggested_refs: 'Mudra', Tallinn, Estonia

stops.name: George Town, Penang: the three turtles
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2015 by es.wikipedia only; the wall within George Town is unlocated, so the coordinates are the historic centre
stops.campa: George Town is a listed port city whose shophouse walls already carry a street-art economy built on light figuration for tourists. He paints three sea turtles into it, hyperrealist and three-dimensional, in a place whose beaches the turtles actually use. His register does not match the local trade: a photograph enlarged onto plaster, standing among drawings made to be posed beside. Sources disagree even on the count, one summary of his career reducing the three turtles to a single one.
suggested_refs: The sea turtle mural, George Town, Penang, Malaysia
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Martín Ron (artista)' (gives three turtles; a derived summary in this research pool reduced them to one, an error flagged not resolved)

stops.name: Puerto de la Cruz, Hay canarios...y canarios
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2015 through the Festival Periplo invitation; no month recorded
stops.campa: Invited by the Festival Periplo to the north coast of Tenerife, he paints Hay canarios...y canarios: a hand with the fingers crossed, built out of his grid, two small birds perched on it. The title is a joke that works only in Spanish and only in these islands, where one word names both the bird and the people. The Canaries have been folding large-scale painting into their tourist self-presentation for years. The year that took him to Estonia and to Malaysia ends on a wall that puns in his own language.
suggested_refs: Festival Periplo, Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife

stops.name: Ciudadela, Parque Cromo under the Acceso Oeste
stops.date_confidence: attested; the date is that of the press report of the intervention in El 1 Digital
stops.campa: On the boundary between Ciudadela and Liniers, where the Acceso Oeste runs on pillars over the street, he directs twenty-five painters colouring the concrete supports. The project is called Parque Cromo. Drivers pass it at ninety kilometres an hour, which sets the terms: no detail survives, only rhythm and colour read in sequence, a park assembled out of columns poured to hold a road up. Directing that many hands under a live motorway is arts administration before it is painting, and arts administration is the degree he took.
suggested_refs: Parque Cromo, pillars of the Acceso Oeste-Perito Moreno between Ciudadela and Liniers
sources: El 1 Digital, 'Intervención artística: pintan los pilares de la autopista entre Ciudadela y Liniers', 3 July 2016

stops.name: Puente Saavedra, painting the underside
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2017 by es.wikipedia, 'Puente Saavedra'; no month recorded, and two research lenses gave coordinates 1.3 km apart for the structure
stops.campa: Where Avenida Cabildo meets the General Paz, on the seam between the capital and the province he was born in, the Puente Saavedra carries traffic across the boundary. He works its lower concrete structure with painted composition: the part of a bridge nobody designs to be seen, the shadowed mass underneath that collects exhaust and torn posters. Nearly everything he paints in the capital stands on one side of that line, and the district that employs him lies on the other. This structure stands on the line itself, carrying traffic between the two.
suggested_refs: Puente Saavedra, Avenida Cabildo at the Avenida General Paz

stops.name: Constitución, Maradona at forty-five metres
stops.date_confidence: October 2022 per press coverage reached only through a search-engine summary; the day is not fixed, so it defaults to 01, and the original articles were not individually verified
stops.campa: On a twelve-storey building at San Juan and Sáenz Peña, in a hard neighbourhood built around a railway terminus, he paints Diego Maradona forty metres wide and forty-five metres high, worked up from a photograph of the 1990 final against Germany. It is unveiled in October 2022, for what would have been the sixty-second birthday, and is reported as the largest portrait of the man anywhere. He says the choice was the combative Diego, the one who went forward. The coverage carrying that line was reached here only in summary, and no article for it could be opened directly.
suggested_refs: The Maradona mural at Av. San Juan and Sáenz Peña, Constitución, Buenos Aires
sources: Press coverage including El País and TyC Sports, reached only through a Brave Search summary; individual article URLs not verified in this research pass

stops.name: Miramar, the water tower
stops.date_confidence: the award is reported in June 2023; the painting itself is not separately dated in the reachable coverage, so the year stands and the month defaults to 01
stops.campa: In a small Atlantic beach town he paints a working water tower thirty-five metres high, wrapping the cylinder in children swimming. The tank goes on holding the town's water throughout; the mural is applied over live infrastructure, not over a decommissioned relic. In 2023 an international street-art platform names it the best mural in the world, an award landing on a resort town rather than a capital. The children in the water have names, and he gives them when asked, along with the holidays they came out of.
stops.quote: Inspirado en las vacaciones en la costa cuando era chico, retraté la esencia de la felicidad a través de la imagen de dos niños, Nina y Salvi deleitándose en un refrescante chapuzón.
stops.quote_source: Martín Ron, quoted in Infobae, 'Un mural de Martín Ron, elegido como el mejor del mundo', 20 June 2023
suggested_refs: The painted water tower at Miramar, Buenos Aires Province; Street Art Cities 'Best Mural in the World' 2023
sources: Infobae, 'Un mural de Martín Ron, elegido como el mejor del mundo', 20 June 2023
Press coverage reached through a Brave Search summary; individual article URLs not verified

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the mural in the wire photograph
stops.date_confidence: attested for the photograph, dated 10 March 2025; the mural's own creation date is not established by any source reachable here
stops.campa: A wire photographer covering the trial of the medical team that treated Diego Maradona in his last weeks files a picture of a Ron mural of him standing in Buenos Aires. The image runs internationally, the painting doing the work of a caption for a story about how he died. Which mural it is, when it went up and where it stands are fixed by no source reachable here. It is widely said to date from around the death in November 2020. That claim is repeated in a great many places and confirmed in none of them reachable here.
suggested_refs: Natacha Pisarenko's Associated Press photograph of a Ron Maradona mural, March 2025
sources: Yahoo News / Associated Press (Natacha Pisarenko), coverage of the trial of Maradona's medical team, 10 March 2025

stops.name: Rosario, Belgrano facing the flag monument
stops.date_confidence: undated; the mural is named only in passing in a July 2025 interview about a different wall, so neither year nor address is established and the year here is a placeholder
stops.campa: A wall in Rosario faces the Monumento a la Bandera, the stone prow raised where Manuel Belgrano first flew the flag over the Paraná. He paints Belgrano onto it, and what he says about the work is a matter of neighbourliness rather than nationhood: he wanted to bring the man back to the barrio, to return him to the place as one more neighbour. The interview carrying those words is chiefly about another mural, four hundred kilometres away, and names this one only in passing.
stops.quote: Quise traerlo al barrio, que volviera al lugar como un vecino más.
stops.quote_source: Martín Ron, quoted in Infobae, 'Con un impactante mural del papa Francisco, Martín Ron completa su trilogía de ídolos populares', 22 July 2025
suggested_refs: The Manuel Belgrano mural at Rosario, near the Monumento Nacional a la Bandera
sources: Infobae, 22 July 2025 (the quotation is verbatim; its attachment to a Belgrano mural in Rosario rests on the article's own framing and was not independently confirmed)

stops.name: La Plata, fifty metres of Bergoglio
stops.date_confidence: attested; the date is that of the Infobae report on the mural in progress
stops.campa: He paints Jorge Bergoglio fifty metres high on the flank of a building in La Plata, the cathedral city an hour southeast of the capital, working through the winter on ropes. Somewhere in the image, as in every wall he has painted, are the words hola, mamá. It began as a message to his mother and stayed; people now come to his finished murals hunting for it, which he did not plan and does not stop. He says he is grateful to have been the one chosen to represent the pope.
stops.quote: Estoy agradecido porque me eligieron para representar al Papa. Es un honor.
stops.quote_source: Martín Ron, quoted in Infobae, 'El espectacular mural de 50 metros de altura que rinde homenaje al Papa Francisco en La Plata', 8 July 2025
suggested_refs: The fifty-metre Pope Francis mural at La Plata, Buenos Aires Province

stops.name: La Plata, the trilogy closed
stops.date_confidence: attested; the date is that of the Infobae report on the finished mural
stops.campa: Two weeks later the wall is finished and the press counts it as the third of a trilogy of popular idols, the pope set beside the footballer and the singer as one more face the country agrees on. He has been painting that agreement for fifteen years: Tévez over his own barrio, Diego Maradona over Constitución, now Bergoglio over La Plata. He calls this one a landmark and says a mural is a living thing, born, ageing and wearing out on the wall like anything else alive.
stops.quote: Los murales tienen una vida: nacen, envejecen, se desgastan. Como la vida misma.
stops.quote_source: Martín Ron, quoted in Infobae, 8 July 2025
suggested_refs: Infobae, 'Con un impactante mural del papa Francisco, Martín Ron completa su trilogía de ídolos populares', 22 July 2025

stops.name: Corrientes and Callao, the Charly García wall
stops.date_confidence: attested; the date is that of the report on the finished mural, the painting having run over the preceding days
stops.campa: At Corrientes and Callao, where the theatre street crosses the avenue and the city agrees to stay awake, he paints Charly García. The face goes up over an intersection that García's own songs have been describing for fifty years, and the traffic below sounds its horns at the scaffolding while the work is going on. He counts the horns in. The street and everything happening on it are part of the piece, he writes when it is done. He has hung work in galleries twice in his life, in Miami and in Mayfair, and it is the walls he writes about.
stops.quote: Gracias a todos los que pasaron, miraron, tocaron bocina, frenaron un rato o compartieron una charla durante estos días de pintura. La calle y todo lo que allí sucede, también forma parte importante de la obra.
stops.quote_source: Martín Ron, posted on social media and quoted in Infobae, 10 May 2026
suggested_refs: The Charly García mural at the corner of Avenida Corrientes and Avenida Callao, Buenos Aires
sources: Infobae, 'El mural de Charly García en la esquina de Corrientes y Callao que transformó el centro de Buenos Aires', 10 May 2026
